resources.string: Open Relay on your phone, on the same Wi-Fi. It shows up here by itself.
Photos, documents, whole folders. They go straight to %1$s.
Connect once to send things to %1$s. You’ll check that both screens show the same shapes.
%1$s is away. What you send now arrives when it’s back.
Check that %1$s shows the same shapes. Only continue if it belongs to you.
Always allow transfers from this device
Make sure %1$s shows these same shapes, then accept there.
From now on it just works. No codes next time.
%1$s didn’t connect. Make sure Relay is open on it and both are on the same Wi-Fi.
%1$s: that didn’t go through. Try again.
%1$s is away. It will be sent when it’s back.
Connection lost. We’ll continue when %1$s is back.
The file arrived damaged, so it wasn’t kept. Try again.
Everything your devices sent to this computer
Files, links and notes your devices send here are kept in this list.
Copy on one device, paste on another: text, images and files, with your trusted devices on the same Wi-Fi.
Start Relay when I sign in
Relay waits in the tray, so your phone can always reach this computer.
Relay %1$s · Protocol v1. Connections are encrypted between your devices. No account, no cloud, no tracking.
A few steps, once. After that they find each other by themselves.
Android: Relay for Android. Windows, Linux and Mac: this app. iPhone and iPad: in the works.
Home Wi-Fi or your phone’s hotspot. No internet needed: devices talk to each other directly.
Click the device and check the shapes
It appears under New nearby. Make sure both screens show the same three shapes, and choose Trust on the other device. Only once.
Choose Allow on private networks. That lets your phone reach this computer on your Wi-Fi. If you missed it: Windows Security › Firewall › Allow an app through the firewall › tick Relay.
Anything you copy here, text, a screenshot or files, is ready to paste on your phone. Files copied on your phone arrive on this clipboard.
Get Relay on your other devices
Relay for desktop on this computer, and Relay for Android on the phone from Google Play.
Put the computer and the phone on the same network. If Windows asks about the firewall, choose Allow on private networks.
The phone appears here under New nearby. Click it, check that both screens show the same three shapes, and tap Trust on the phone.
Copy on one, paste on the other. Drag a file to the drop shelf on the left edge of this screen and drop it on the phone, or share to this computer from the phone.
Both phones need the app from Google Play. Either one can start the connection.
Join both phones to the same Wi-Fi. No Wi-Fi around? Turn on one phone’s hotspot and connect the other to it; no internet needed.
On either phone, tap the other under New nearby. Check that both screens show the same three shapes, then tap Trust on the second phone.
Share photos and files between them from any app, and hold the two phones back to back to swap contact cards.
Install Relay for desktop on both
Download it from GitHub for Windows or Linux and run it on each computer. It sits in the system tray.
Both computers on the same Wi-Fi or the same wired network. Allow Relay through the firewall on private networks.
On one computer, click the other under New nearby. Check that both screens show the same three shapes, then choose Trust on the second computer.
Copy on one computer and paste on the other, or drag files onto the drop shelf at the left edge of the screen.
Anything your trusted devices send or drop here arrives straight away, with no Accept button, and is ready to paste.
A slim tab on the left edge of the screen. Drag any file or text onto it, then drop it on a device.
Pair a device to drop files on it.
Drag and drop to your phone
Drag a file to the left edge of the screen. The drop shelf opens with your devices: drop it on your phone and it arrives there, ready to paste. Trusted devices never ask you to accept.
Nothing to send. Copy some text and keep a trusted device nearby.
Relay is already running. Look for it in the system tray.
